v283: TIMELINE UNIFICATION 2c — THE READING ROOM IS RETIRED. The owner ruled (2026-09-03, R4a of the timeline-unification decision record) that Go Dig, Go Deep and the Reading Room were one idea that evolved and never achieved what it was for; Add Landmark (Cut 6, planned) replaces this line of work. This release removes it entirely: the `reading_room` child interaction (`interactions/reading_room/`, 19 files), `system/reading_room.py`, `system/reading_room_evals.py`, `tests/test_reading_room.py`, and the research corpus `system/research/go-deep.md`; the `reading-room-plan`/`reading-room-evals` CLI verbs; `timeline.dig_plan` and its supporting machinery (`DIG_PLAN_SIZE`, the witness/precision-grade constants, `witness_for`/`precision_target_for`/`precision_ask`/`witness_question`/`render_dig_list`/`_living_roster`/`_entity_reach`/`_ref_reach`/`_witness_matcher`/`_open_landmark_domains`/`_entity_type`); the `data["reading_room"]` block and `counts.reading_room_asks` from `timeline.timeline_data()`; `conversation_delivery.TurnShape.reading_room_stage` and its four output-contract gates; the `reading_room` row in `interactions/registry.json`; and `wiki_compile.py`'s `dig_lists_by_slug`/`apply_dig_lists`, which read the now-gone plan. `timeline.keystones()`, `_scored_anchors()` and `_greedy_plan()` — the greedy-over-the-residual mechanism the Reading Room extended rather than owned — are UNCHANGED; `_greedy_plan` sheds the `width`/`universe` kwargs only the Reading Room's extension used. `timeline.unknown_width` (ADR 0027's placement-score arithmetic) is UNCHANGED and stays. Cross-dating (ADR 0026), the placement score (ADR 0027) and the landmark recorder (ADR 0028) are unaffected — nothing in the fold depended on the Reading Room's own code. `chronology.py`'s witness-provenance mechanism (`witness_provenance`, `witness_slug`, `witness_name`, the three EVIDENCE bases) is general infrastructure the Reading Room used but did not own, and stays. ADR 0025 gets a dated "Retired 2026-09-03 (owner)" note at its top; its body is unedited. `docs/handbook/interactions/reading-room.md` and `docs/pr-specs/reading-room.md` are deleted; the handbook index, the glossary, `interactions/README.md`'s child-interaction table (seven children -> six) and README references are updated to match. `system/research/QUEUE.md`'s "Go Deep" backlog section is removed (a live, unworked queue — nothing in it was ever ingested). Every remaining docstring, research-doc and pr-spec citation of go-deep.md's specific sections is re-pointed at ADR 0025/0026/0027 or dated 2026-09-03; `interactions/landmarks/evals/lints.yaml` and `interactions/timeline/evals/lints.yaml`'s `never_proposes_a_date` citations move the same way. `interactions/registry.json` and the `interaction_registry`/`test_timeline_interaction` registry tests now list six children of `conversation`, not seven. v280: TIMELINE ERAS E-L3 — GO DIG GETS A REAL WRITE PATH. Until this release the residences/schools/work ladder had no way to take a whole paste — a person's own written history of homes, schools and jobs — and file it as real vault facts; every entry had to come one conversational turn at a time. `go-dig-record` files ONE structured unit through `timeline.save_landmark` — the SAME writer `landmark-record` and the recorder's own `landmark_invocations` already call, never a second one — with the additive fields E-L2c shipped (`approximate`, `ongoing`, `place_ref`, `nickname`, `link`, `address`): a place name resolves or mints the roster entity, a nickname files a roster alias decision (a colliding alias binds to neither and mints one `identity_uncertain` item naming both), and an optional free-text note is promoted as its own owner-only `type: go_dig_note` source carrying the unit's own stay as its `question_context` — so a moment later classified from that note is filed `part_of` the stay by the SAME deterministic rung event identity already ships (12b.5), proved here through the real binder with a synthetic classified moment.

`go-dig-import` reads a whole pasted document and parses it with a DETERMINISTIC, MODEL-FREE grammar (`go_dig_grammar.py`, design §10.6): blank-line-separated blocks, `Dates: START - END` with per-bound `[…]` approximate brackets and `now`/`present` for an open stay, `City/State`/`City/Country`/`Kanton/Country`/`Country` place forms with the finer key winning and `located_in` filed on the region, `Nickname` with its trailing parenthetical stripped to the note, `Address`/`Link` (`https:` only) verbatim, `School` (`None`/blank/`Done`/a name with a trailing grade phrase split even without a comma), `Work` (`None`/blank/comma-separated items with an inline org, an `in place` clause and inline `(start …)`/`(end …)` dates), and `Events` falling to the note untouched — nothing in it is parsed by the import. A job or school listed under a stay is NOT dated by that stay: it files its own bounded start/end claims at `basis: order`/`confidence: inferred` with a provenance clause naming the stay it was listed under (`chronology.CALCULATED_PROVENANCE_BASIS`), never the stay's own dates as stated bounds — a stated inline date always wins over the inferred one. Consecutive listings of the identical wording merge into one tenure through the existing interval-aware ladder key; a CHANGED wording at one organization (\"Boeing\" then \"Boeing in Seattle\") stays two tenures — one roster organization, two entries — because the wording difference is carried into the entry's own `label` rather than erased by the grammar's own where-extraction.

`--preview` parses and reports — every block's parsed fields, what fell to the note, its `ready`/`needs_a_hand` status, and any consecutive-stay overlap over three months — and writes nothing; `--apply --import-operation-id <id>` files every block in order. Identity for an imported unit is `(import_operation_id, block content digest, unit kind, discriminator)` — never the filing ordinal, which shifts on every retry as earlier blocks land — so a crash after N blocks and a re-run under the same id files the rest and mints nothing twice, and a re-ordered paste of the same blocks (block content digests are order-independent by construction) mints nothing new either. A malformed block is reported `needs_a_hand` and skipped while every valid block still files. Zero model calls anywhere in the import path — asserted by an AST sweep of the two new modules' own imports, not a runtime mock — because a note's own moments classify LATER, as an ordinary targeted job under the tenant's budget.

Under the hood: `landmark_projection.promote_landmark_entry`/`file_landmark_record` gain an optional `digest` override (byte-identical when omitted); `timeline.save_landmark` gains `digest_override` threading to it; `temporal_store.promote_conversational_source` gains an optional `source_type` (defaulting to its existing `conversation_message`, byte-identical for every other caller) so a Go Dig note can carry `type: go_dig_note` while reusing the SAME storage path, digest and `question_context` mechanics whole. New: `system/go_dig_grammar.py` (pure parsing), `system/go_dig_writer.py` (the writer and the import), both registered as `DIRECT_MUTATION_COMMANDS` in `lifehug.py`. `tests/test_go_dig.py` covers the grammar's every field form on a synthetic worked example, the writer's roster/alias/note-promotion behavior, and the import's crash-retry, malformed-block, reorder, inherited-window, changed-wording and school-closure promises (design §12 rows 15, 16, 25, 28, 31–35) plus the row-35 containment proof through the real `episode_binder`.

Deviations named rather than silently narrowed: the platform contract's own Launch-and-verify sketch names a `fixtures/go-dig/synthetic-paste.txt` path this repository has never had a `fixtures/` convention for (no such directory exists anywhere in the tree); the synthetic worked example lives instead as a committed constant in `tests/test_go_dig.py::BlockGrammarTests.EXAMPLE`, covered by its own round-trip test rather than invented as a new top-level layout. `landmark_entry_key`'s identity for a domain with no `label` reads only `label`/`name` and never a domain's own identity rung (`city`/`what`) — a gap this release's writer works around by defaulting `label` from the identity rung when the caller does not set one, rather than by widening `landmark_entry_key`/`identity_named` themselves, which is a bigger, separate change than this program's bounded writer/import scope and is named here for a future PR to pick up.

v279: TIMELINE ERAS E-L2d — THE TIMELINE SAYS HOW IT KNOWS WHEN, AND A DECADE CAN BE TOLD BY ITS ERAS. Until this release a thing on your Timeline carried its time in one of four different fields and said nothing about which. A story you never dated, placed inside the five years you lived in one house, carried that house's whole span — correctly, as bounds — and any surface that measured it drew a five-year bar for an afternoon. Every published thing now carries one word for how its time is known: a **duration** (a decade of your life, a stay, a job — a bar), a **point** (something that happened, a mark exactly as wide as the grain you gave it and never wider), a **window** (no date of its own, only the stretch it must have fallen inside — drawn hollow, never as a bar) or **none** (not placed yet). It is derived from what is already there, so nothing can set it to something it is not, and a window never counts as width toward how placed your life is.

AND YOUR DECADES CAN NOW BE TOLD BY THEIR ERAS — WHEN YOU SAY SO. If the eras you have dated cover a decade between them, the frame's row offers one line: tell My 20s by its eras? One tap files a decision and the era rows stand on their own; undo files another decision and puts the frame back. Nothing is ever applied for you: there is no coverage percentage anywhere, an era you have not dated never counts toward it, and neither does a thread like Fatherhood, which has no honest end. The years no era claims are published so the page can draw them under the frame's own name. `lifehug frame-display` is the door and `--undo` is the way back; both are idempotent, and neither moves a single date.

Under the hood: `temporal_projection.derive_value_shape` / `VALUE_SHAPES` / `LANES_BY_EVENT_KIND` / `validate_lane_row`; the projection's schema-v3 writer flag `LIFEHUG_PROJECTION_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`projection_schema_version()`, default 2 — v2 output is byte-identical, rollback is the flag), which at 3 adds `value_shape` on nodes, `lanes` per row group (Lived · Worked · Schooled) and `frame_display` per frame; `cross_dating.frame_tiling` / `FRAME_TILING_RULE_TEXT` as the one half-open, grain-honest tiling arithmetic; `era_memberships.file_frame_display` and its digest, supersession and readers; `temporal_timeline.lane_rows` / `frame_display_rows` in the fold and inside `structural_signature`; `temporal_publication.calculated_view` as the tolerant reader plus `RESERVED_SCHEMA_V3_KEYS` for E-L2c's `coverage`/`closures`. The rebuild oracle `temporal_publication.verify` now folds the four inputs the publisher folds and it did not before — membership assertions, display decisions, frame display decisions and landmark entries — so on any vault holding one of them it re-derived a different projection and reported the publication broken. ADR 0030 gains the E-L2d addendum.
